## Beam Buying Guide

### How do I measure for a ceiling beam or a mantel?
For a ceiling beam, measure the length the beam should cover, and note the ceiling height and which way the joists run. Solid and box beams come in 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft lengths, and other lengths are available by quote. For a mantel, measure the fireplace opening and the overhang you want on each side; stock mantels have an 8 inch face, are 10 inches deep, and run 6 to 10 ft. Send those measurements with the free quote form so we can price the length you need.

### Should I choose a box beam or a solid beam?
Choose a box beam if you want the look of a timber on a finished ceiling and you need something much lighter than solid wood. A box beam is a three-sided hollow beam, open on top, so it slides over a mounting board. A solid beam is 8 by 8 or 10 by 10 inches and it's heavy, so plan for proper support and a carpenter or builder to install it. Both are decorative unless your builder or a structural engineer approves the piece to carry a load.

### How are beams mounted?
Box beams are usually mounted by screwing a wood board, called blocking, into the ceiling joists, then sliding the beam over it and fastening through the sides. Mantels are usually hung on a hidden steel bracket or on lag bolts set into studs or masonry. Solid beams are heavy, so plan the support before they go up. We recommend a carpenter or builder for the install.

### How do I pick a stain to match my floors or cabinets?
Beams, mantels, and tables come in a natural (clear), medium, or dark finish. Hold a sample of your floor or cabinet color next to those three and pick the closest one. Reclaimed wood won't match another finish exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. If you're between two tones, describe the floors and cabinets on the free quote form and tell us which finish you want. For contrast or blend, painted and stained cabinets, trim, doors, and lighting, see how to match a reclaimed beam to your floors, cabinets and trim at https://barndobeamco.com/#finish-matching-guide.

### How long does a custom order take, and how does a quote work?
Every piece is made to order, so the timing depends on the size and the wood available, and we give you an estimated time with your quote. Use the free quote form, or call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), and tell us the piece, the size, the finish, and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the price and shipping, and you're under no obligation. Once you approve the quote, you can pay securely online by card, and we send photos before your piece ships.

### Do you ship beams, and how are they packed?
Yes, we ship to every state in the continental US by freight or ground carrier, depending on size and weight, and each piece is packed with care. Shipping is quoted to your ZIP code before you pay. Put your ZIP on the free quote form and the shipping price comes back with the wood price.

### How do I clean and care for a hand-hewn beam?
Dust the beam with a soft, dry cloth, and wipe spills promptly so water doesn't sit on the wood. Don't soak the beam or use harsh cleaners, because they can dull a natural, medium, or dark finish. The adze marks, nail holes, and weathered color are part of the wood, so clean the surface and leave the texture as it is. If you have a question about the finish after it arrives, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326) or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to.

### Can I get a table that matches my beams?
Yes, we make dining, coffee, and console tables to order from the same hand-hewn reclaimed beams, in a natural, medium, or dark finish. Tell us the size, the finish, and your room, and mention any mantel or ceiling beams you want it to sit with. No two pieces of reclaimed wood match exactly. We'll send a free quote with shipping to your ZIP code.

## Fireplace mantel sizing guide

How to size a reclaimed wood fireplace mantel: measure the firebox, add overhang, then match a stock length. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-guide

### How do I size a reclaimed wood fireplace mantel?
Measure the width of the firebox opening in inches, then add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side. That total is the mantel length. Stock mantels from Barndo Beam Co. have an 8 inch face, are 10 inches deep, and come in 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 ft lengths, from about $1,050. If the math lands between stock lengths, round up to the next length, or request a custom length. The shortest stock mantel is 6 ft, so a smaller firebox simply gets a little more overhang. Send the firebox width, the length, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote for the wood price and shipping.

### How much should a fireplace mantel overhang the firebox?
Add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side of the firebox opening. Six inches looks tighter. Twelve inches looks heavier and suits a thick reclaimed beam. A 48 inch firebox plus 12 inches on each side is 72 inches, which is a 6 ft mantel. A 60 inch firebox plus 12 inches on each side is 84 inches, which is a 7 ft mantel. A 36 inch firebox is shorter than the 6 ft stock minimum, so a 6 ft mantel leaves about 18 inches of overhang on each side. Measure the firebox opening, inside edge to inside edge.

### Should I choose a mantel beam or a full fireplace surround?
Choose a mantel beam when you only need the shelf across the top. A stock mantel is 8 inches tall by 10 inches deep, in 6 to 10 ft lengths. Choose a one-of-a-kind mantel beam when you want to approve photos of one exact beam before it is cut. The face is usually 8 to 10 inches, and lengths start at 6 ft. Choose a full beam fireplace surround when you want a mantel plus two legs, three matching beams that frame the opening. Surrounds are available, and custom sizes are quoted. Finishes are natural (clear), medium, or dark. Request a free quote with your ZIP code and we reply within 2 business days with the price and shipping.

### What stock mantel sizes are available?
Stock reclaimed wood mantels have an 8 inch tall face and are 10 inches deep. Lengths are 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 ft, and a 6 ft mantel starts at about $1,050. Lengths longer than 10 ft are available by quote. A full beam fireplace surround, a mantel plus two legs, is available too. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US. Finishes are natural (clear), medium, or dark.

## Dining table sizing guide

How to size a custom reclaimed wood dining table: match seats to a length, pick a width and a base, then request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#table-guide

### How do I size a custom reclaimed wood dining table?
Count the seats, then match a length. Allow about 24 inches of table length per person. A custom reclaimed wood dining table from Barndo Beam Co. is usually 36 inches (3 ft) or 42 inches (3.5 ft) wide. Four seats fit a 5 or 6 ft table. Six seats fit a 6 or 7 ft table. Eight seats fit an 8 ft table. Ten seats fit a 10 ft table. Twelve seats fit a 12 ft table. Rectangular farmhouse tables run 5 to 12 ft, from about $3,150. Choose a trestle, beam legs, or a beam top on steel, then a natural, medium, or dark finish. Send the seat count, the length, the width, the base, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote. Every table is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

### How long should a reclaimed wood dining table be for 4, 6, 8, 10, or 12 people?
Allow about 24 inches of length per person. Four people fit a 5 or 6 ft table. Six people fit a 6 or 7 ft table. Eight people fit an 8 ft table. Ten people fit a 10 ft table. Twelve people fit a 12 ft table. Barndo Beam Co. builds rectangular reclaimed wood dining tables in those lengths, 36 or 42 inches wide, handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

### How wide should a custom dining table be?
A rectangular reclaimed wood dining table is usually 36 inches (3 ft) or 42 inches (3.5 ft) wide. Thirty-six inches seats one person on each side. Forty-two inches leaves room for serving dishes down the center. Leave about 36 inches of walkway behind each chair. Round and square tables from Barndo Beam Co. run 3 to 7 ft across.

### What is the difference between a trestle, beam legs, and a beam top on steel?
A trestle has two end supports joined by a stretcher, so chairs slide in along the sides. Beam legs are thick hand-hewn posts, the same timber face as a mantel. A beam top on steel keeps the reclaimed wood top and uses a black steel base. Barndo Beam Co. builds all three to order. Tell us which base you want when you request a free quote.

### How do I match a dining table to my existing beams or mantel?
Order the table in the same finish as the beams or mantel: natural (clear), medium, or dark. The table is built from the same hand-hewn reclaimed wood. No two pieces match exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. Name the mantel or beam finish on the free quote form, and we send photos of your table before it ships.

We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free, and every table is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

A custom reclaimed wood coffee table is usually about 16 to 18 inches tall, level with the sofa seat or an inch or two lower. Make the length about one-half to two-thirds of the sofa, and leave 12 to 18 inches of walkway on the open sides. ### How tall should a reclaimed wood coffee table be next to a sofa?
A reclaimed wood coffee table is usually about 16 to 18 inches tall, level with the sofa seat or an inch or two lower. Measure from the floor to the top of the seat cushion and set the table at that height or slightly under it. An 8 ft sofa pairs with a table about 48 to 64 inches long. Leave 12 to 18 inches of walkway between the table and the sofa, and on any side people walk past. Stock coffee tables from Barndo Beam Co. are 2 x 3, 2 x 4, 3 x 4, 3 x 5, 3 x 6, 4 x 6, 4 x 7, and 5 x 8 ft.

## Ceiling beam sizing and spacing guide

How to size and space decorative ceiling beams: match the face to the ceiling height and the span, set the on-center spacing, count the beams, then request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide

### What size ceiling beam should I use for my ceiling height and room width?
Match the face of a decorative ceiling beam to the ceiling height, then to the span. On a ceiling about 8 to 9 feet high, an 8 by 8 inch beam is the stock solid size. On a ceiling about 9 to 12 feet high, 8 by 8 is the usual size. On a ceiling about 12 feet or taller, or across a wide great room, use a 10 by 10. For the span the beam crosses, an 8 by 8 suits a run up to about 16 ft, and a 10 by 10 suits a run of about 18 to 20 ft. Stock solid and box beams from Barndo Beam Co. come in 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft lengths. Space the beams about 3, 4, or 6 feet on center. A face larger than 10 by 10, or another length, is available by quote. These sizes are for a decorative beam. If the beam has to carry a load, have your builder or a structural engineer approve it first. Send the ceiling height, the room size, the beam count, solid or box, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote. Every beam is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

### How far apart should decorative ceiling beams be spaced?
Space decorative ceiling beams about 3, 4, or 6 feet on center. On center means from the center of one beam to the center of the next. About 3 feet on center is a tighter rhythm, and it suits a kitchen. About 4 feet on center is the usual spacing in a living room or great room with 8 by 8 beams. About 6 feet on center is a more open ceiling, and it pairs well with a 10 by 10 so each beam still reads. To space them evenly, divide the width you are spacing across by the number of beams. That result is the on-center spacing, and the center of the first and last beam sits half of that spacing in from each side wall. A room 12 ft across with 3 beams is 4 ft on center. A room 16 ft across with 4 beams is 4 ft on center. A room 20 ft across with 5 beams is 4 ft on center.

### How many ceiling beams do I need for a common room?
Run the beams the long way and space them across the short way. A 12 by 12 ft room takes 3 beams, each 12 ft, at 4 ft on center. A matched package of 3 beams by 12 ft is $5,400, and a single solid 12 ft beam is $1,920. A 12 by 16 ft room takes 3 beams, each 16 ft, spaced across the 12 ft side at 4 ft on center. A matched package of 3 beams by 16 ft is $7,200. A 16 by 20 ft room takes 4 beams, each 20 ft, spaced across the 16 ft side at 4 ft on center. A solid 20 ft beam is $3,200, and a box beam at 20 ft is $3,300. A room 20 ft across takes 5 beams at 4 ft on center. A matched package of 5 beams by 20 ft is $15,000. Packages are matched for color and texture, 8 by 8 standard, at $150 per foot. Send the room size and your ZIP code with a free quote.

### Should I choose a solid hand-hewn beam or a hollow box beam for a ceiling?
Choose a solid hand-hewn beam when you want a full timber, 8 by 8 or 10 by 10 inches. It is solid wood and heavy, so plan the support with a carpenter or builder before it goes up. A solid beam is $1,280 at 8 ft, $1,920 at 12 ft, $2,560 at 16 ft, and $3,200 at 20 ft. Choose a box beam when you want the look of a timber on a finished ceiling and you need something much lighter. A box beam is a three-sided hollow beam, open on top, so it slides over a wood mounting board screwed into the joists, then fastens through the sides. A box beam is $1,320 at 8 ft, $1,980 at 12 ft, $2,640 at 16 ft, and $3,300 at 20 ft. Custom widths are by quote, which helps on a lower ceiling. Both are decorative unless your builder or a structural engineer approves the piece to carry a load.

### Which finish should I choose for ceiling beams?
Ceiling beams come in a natural (clear), medium, or dark finish, the same three finishes as mantels and tables. Natural keeps the weathered color of the reclaimed wood. Medium warms it. Dark deepens the grain and sits well with black window frames and iron. Hold a sample of your floor or cabinet color next to those three and pick the closest one. Reclaimed wood won't match another finish exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. Name the finish on the free quote form, and we send photos before the beams ship.

### How do I measure for ceiling beams?
Measure the ceiling height from the finished floor to the finished ceiling. Measure the span each beam will cover, wall to wall, in the direction the beams will run. That number is the beam length. Measure the other direction, the width you will space the beams across. Note which way the joists run. Beams usually run across the joists so the mounting board can fasten into them. Note lights, fans, and soffits the beams have to clear. Stock lengths are 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft. If the span falls between those, round up to the next stock length or ask for a custom length. Send the height, the length, the width, the beam count, and your ZIP code with a free quote.

### How do I request a free quote for ceiling beams?
Use the free quote form, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Include the ceiling height, the beam length, the width you are spacing across, the beam count, the on-center spacing, solid or box, the size (8 by 8 or 10 by 10), the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free, and every beam is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

## Reclaimed beam care and finish guide

How to clean, finish, and care for a hand-hewn reclaimed beam, mantel, or beam table top: dust it dry, pick a finish, leave normal checks, keep it out of direct weather, follow the fireplace maker's mantel clearance, and request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide

### How do I clean and dust a hand-hewn reclaimed beam or mantel?
Dust a hand-hewn reclaimed beam or mantel with a soft, dry cloth, a lambswool duster, or a vacuum with a soft brush on low. Work along the grain. The adze marks, nail holes, and weathered color are part of the wood, so clean the surface and leave the texture. For a fingerprint or a light mark, wipe with a barely damp cloth and dry the spot at once. Do not soak the beam. Do not use a steam mop, bleach, ammonia, or a harsh cleaner, because they can dull a natural, medium, or dark finish. Do not sand the face. Sanding removes the hand-hewn marks.

### What is the difference between a raw beam, a clear matte sealer, an oil finish, and a light stain?
A raw beam has no film on the wood. You see the weathered gray-brown, the checks, and the tool marks, and water can spot it. A clear matte sealer is a thin clear coat with almost no shine, so the color stays close to the raw beam and a spill beads instead of soaking in at once. That is the look of a natural (clear) finish. An oil soaks in, deepens the amber and the grain, and stays low in sheen. It is not a hard film, and an oiled top can take a thin coat again later. A light stain is a thin warm tint, lighter than a medium or dark stain, and the checks and adze marks still show. Beams, mantels, and tables from Barndo Beam Co. are finished natural (clear), medium, or dark before they ship. Natural is the clear look. Medium warms the wood. Dark deepens the grain. Name the finish on the free quote form. Reclaimed wood will not match another finish exactly.

### Are checks and cracks normal in old reclaimed wood?
Yes. A check is a split that follows the grain. Old hand-hewn beams checked as they dried, often decades ago, and a check, a nail hole, or a small crack in the face is normal in reclaimed wood. It does not mean a decorative beam is failing. Wood also moves a little when indoor humidity changes, so a hairline check can open in the first heating season. Leave the checks. Filler can pop out when the wood moves. If a piece arrives broken, or a crack runs across the beam rather than along the grain, send photos within 48 hours to barndobeamco@agentmail.to or call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326).

### Can I use a reclaimed beam indoors or on a covered porch?
Use a reclaimed beam indoors, or on a covered porch where the roof keeps rain off it. A porch or entry header is for that covered spot. Keep the beam out of direct weather. Do not set it where rain, a sprinkler, or standing water hits the wood. Direct weather swells the beam, opens checks, and wears a finish off. Indoors, dust the beam and keep standing water off it. Every beam is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

### How much heat clearance does a wood fireplace mantel need?
Follow your local building code and the clearance listed by the fireplace maker. A wood mantel is combustible. The safe distance from the firebox opening to the wood is set by that listing and by local code. Read the fireplace manual, and have the installer confirm the mantel height before the beam goes up. If the listing is missing, do not guess. Ask the installer or the local building office. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood mantel. The fireplace maker's clearance is the one to follow.

### How do I care for a reclaimed beam table top?
Use coasters under glasses, bottles, and plants. Wipe a spill right away, especially water, wine, or oil, then dry the spot. Do not set a hot pan on the wood, and do not use a soaking cloth. On an oiled top, re-oil when water stops beading or the surface looks dry: wipe on a thin coat, let it soak in, and wipe off all of the extra oil. On a clear sealed top, or a bar top with a sealed bar finish, dust and wipe. Do not strip a sealer to re-oil it. Tell us if the top is for dining when you request a free quote, and include your ZIP code.

### How do I request a free quote for a beam, mantel, or beam table?
Use the free quote form, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Tell us the piece (a ceiling beam, a mantel, a porch header, or a table), the size, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

## Mantel install guide

How to install a reclaimed beam mantel: find the studs or solid masonry, check that the wall is level, set the height from local building code and the fireplace or insert manufacturer, choose a hidden steel bracket, a cleat lagged into studs, or masonry anchors, plan for the weight of a solid beam, and request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-install-guide

### What are the common ways to mount a reclaimed beam mantel?
Three mounts are common. A hidden steel bracket, or steel rods, is drilled into the back of the beam so the hardware stays out of sight. A wood cleat is fastened with lag screws into the wall studs, and the mantel sits on that cleat. On a brick or stone fireplace, masonry anchors go into the solid masonry, not into drywall. Pick the mount that matches the wall. A carpenter should do the install. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood mantel, and the mantel is decorative.

### How do I find studs or blocking for a mantel?
Find the studs with a stud finder, then confirm each center. Studs are often 16 inches apart, and sometimes 24. Mark the centers where the mantel will sit. The fasteners have to land in studs or in solid wood blocking, not in drywall alone. If the studs miss the spots that need to carry the beam, a carpenter can add blocking. On a finished wall, line the bracket or the cleat up with the studs you found. Do not use drywall anchors for a solid beam.

### How do I check that the fireplace wall is level before I hang a mantel?
Hold a long level where the mantel will sit. Check side to side, so the shelf will be level, and check the wall face, so the beam will not tilt out at one end. Brick and stone are often uneven. Shim behind the cleat or the bracket so the mantel reads level even when the stone does not. Check the mantel with the level again before the last fasteners are tightened. Drill the holes in the back of the beam only after the height and the level are set.

### How heavy is a solid reclaimed beam mantel, and can the wall hold it?
A solid reclaimed mantel is real timber, not a hollow box. A longer beam weighs more than a shorter one, and a thicker beam weighs more than a thinner one. Plan on two or more people to lift it, and have a carpenter or builder do the install. The weight has to go into wall studs or into solid masonry. Drywall, a thin stone veneer that is only stuck to the wall, and plastic anchors are not the support. If you are not sure the wall can hold the beam, stop and ask a carpenter before you drill. Each reclaimed beam is a different piece of wood, so there is no single weight for every mantel. Ask for the weight of your beam on the free quote if your carpenter needs it, and include your ZIP code.

### How much clearance does a combustible mantel need above the firebox?
Clearance above the firebox for a combustible mantel is set by your local building code and by the fireplace or insert manufacturer. Check both. A wood mantel is combustible. Read the manual for that fireplace or insert, and confirm the clearance with the local building office or your installer. If the manual and the local code do not match, follow the stricter one. Do not copy a height from a photo, and do not guess a number. Set the mantel height only after that clearance is known. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood mantel. The code and the fireplace maker set the clearance.

### Should a homeowner install a reclaimed beam mantel?
A homeowner can plan the job: find the studs, check that the wall is level, read the fireplace or insert manual, and check local building code. Hanging the beam is a carpenter's job on most walls, because a solid beam is heavy and the fasteners have to hit studs or solid masonry. If the fireplace is an insert, follow that manufacturer's instructions as well as local code. We recommend a carpenter or builder for the install.

### How do I request a free quote for a reclaimed wood mantel?
Use the free quote form, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Tell us the mantel length, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), whether the wall is framed, brick, or stone, and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free. Every mantel is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

## Holiday mantel styling guide

How to decorate a reclaimed beam mantel for the holidays: layer greenery, candles, and stockings, hang stockings with weighted holders so the wood stays unmarked, keep flammables away from a working fireplace, follow the fireplace manufacturer and local code, and request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#holiday-mantel-guide

### How do I decorate a reclaimed beam mantel for the holidays?
Layer a reclaimed beam mantel from the wall outward. Set garland or greenery along the back of the shelf so it does not drape into the firebox. Place candles or small objects in front of the greenery, and hang stockings off the front edge. Leave the center of the firebox clear. A stock mantel is 10 inches deep, so plan one row, not a deep display. Use battery candles on the wood. If you use real candles, keep them in sturdy holders, keep them off the greenery, and never leave them burning unattended. Keep every flammable away from the fire, and follow the fireplace or insert manufacturer and your local code. Do not guess a clearance number. Every mantel from Barndo Beam Co. is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

### How do I hang stockings on a solid wood beam mantel without damaging it?
Use weighted stocking holders. The weight sits on the shelf and the hook drops over the front edge, so you do not drill the beam. Set the weight toward the back of the 10 inch shelf so a full stocking does not tip the holder. Hang the stockings beside the firebox opening, not across it, and keep them clear of candles and greenery. A small screw hook or nail leaves a hole that stays. If you use a small hook, put it on the underside near the front edge, and keep it off the hand-hewn face. Do not drill the back of the beam where a hidden bracket or rods may already sit. Skip adhesive hooks. They can pull a natural, medium, or dark finish off when you remove them. After the holidays, lift the weighted holders off and the wood is unchanged.

### How much clearance do candles and greenery need from a working fireplace?
Keep flammables away from a working fireplace and away from any flame. Greenery, dried branches, ribbons, paper, and stockings can burn, and a wood mantel is combustible too. The safe distance from the firebox opening to the wood is set by your local building code and by the fireplace or insert manufacturer. Decorations follow that same rule. Do not hang greenery, a stocking, or a ribbon into the firebox or into the clearance the manual requires. Do not guess a number of inches, and do not copy a distance from a photo. Read the fireplace or insert manual, and follow local code. If they do not match, follow the stricter one. Battery candles remove the open flame from the shelf. If you burn the fireplace, keep the mantel clear of anything that can fall, swing, or drip into the opening, and do not leave real candles lit. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood mantel. The fireplace maker and local code set the clearance.

### How do I choose mantel length and depth before the holidays?
Measure the firebox opening, inside edge to inside edge, then add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side. That total is the mantel length. The overhang is where the end stockings hang, so they sit beside the opening instead of across it. Stock mantels from Barndo Beam Co. have an 8 inch tall face and are 10 inches deep, in 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 ft lengths. Ten inches of depth holds one layer of garland plus stocking holders. If the math lands between stock lengths, round up to the next length, or ask for a custom length. A deeper shelf is a custom size by quote. The wood still has to clear the firebox by whatever your local code and the fireplace maker require. See how to size a reclaimed wood fireplace mantel at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-guide and how to install a reclaimed beam mantel at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-install-guide.

### When should I order a reclaimed wood mantel for the holidays?
Order early for the holidays. Every mantel is made to order, so the timing depends on the size and the wood available. Ask about current lead times in your free quote. The estimate comes back with the quote. This page does not promise a date. Send the mantel length, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. Every mantel is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped in the continental US.

## Hand-hewn vs. resawn vs. faux beam guide

How to tell real reclaimed wood: read the face for adze or broad-axe marks, circular or band saw marks, or a faux beam of new lumber or foam, then check nail holes, mortise pockets, checks, patina, and weight. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#hewn-vs-faux-guide

### What does hand-hewn mean on a reclaimed wood beam?
Hand-hewn means the faces were shaped with an adze or a broad axe, not with a saw. An adze leaves short scooped cuts. A broad axe leaves longer facets. The cuts overlap and change direction, so the face is uneven, with high spots and low spots, and the edges wander. A hewn face does not show repeating circular arcs or straight parallel saw lines. The end of a beam is often sawn square when it is cut to length. Read the long faces, not that end cut.

### How is resawn or rough-sawn reclaimed wood different from hand-hewn?
Resawn wood is old timber cut again on a saw. Rough-sawn means the saw texture was left on the face instead of being planed smooth. A circular saw leaves repeating arcs across the face. A band saw leaves fine, fairly straight, parallel lines. The face is flatter and more even than a hand-hewn face. The timber can still be old. Nail holes, checks, and gray patina can remain on a surface that was not resawn, while the fresh-sawn face looks lighter and shows the saw pattern. Saw marks alone do not prove the wood is old.

### What do faux beams made of new lumber or foam look like?
A faux beam imitates a timber. A new-lumber box is flat boards joined into a U-shape or a hollow rectangle. The faces are flat, the edges are crisp and square, the grain looks new, and the stain is often one even brown. It has no old nail holes, mortise pockets, or deep checks, and it is much lighter than solid timber of the same outside size. Molded foam is lighter still. The texture can repeat, the color is paint on the surface, it sounds thin when tapped, and it can flex or dent. A hollow box can still be real reclaimed wood. A Barndo Beam Co. hand-hewn box beam is three-sided, made from reclaimed wood that still shows adze and axe marks, and it is not foam and not new lumber.

### What are the signs of real age in reclaimed wood?
Look for nail holes or spike holes, often with dark iron stain, and for mortise pockets, peg holes, or notches where the timber joined a frame. A check is a split that follows the grain, left as the beam dried. Patina is uneven gray, amber, and brown that sits down in the tool marks, not one even coat of stain on the surface. Weight is the other test. Solid old timber is heavy for its size. Foam of the same outside size is light, and a new-lumber box falls in between. Each reclaimed beam is different, so ask for the weight of the piece you are buying.

### Should I choose a hand-hewn beam, resawn reclaimed wood, or a faux beam for a mantel, ceiling, or table?
Choose hand-hewn reclaimed wood for a fireplace mantel, a feature ceiling beam, or a table people will touch. The uneven face and the axe marks hold up at close range. Solid beams are heavy, so plan support with a carpenter. Choose resawn or rough-sawn reclaimed wood when you want a flatter face for a table top or a straighter ceiling line, and confirm the timber is actually old. Choose a faux beam of new lumber or foam only for a lightweight decorative ceiling seen from across the room. It will not pass a close look on a mantel or a table. Barndo Beam Co. beams, mantels, and tables are hand-hewn reclaimed wood, handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US. They are decorative unless a builder or a structural engineer approves a piece to carry a load.

### What questions should I ask before I buy a reclaimed beam?
Ask whether the face was shaped with an adze or a broad axe, or cut on a circular saw or a band saw. Ask whether the piece is solid timber, a hollow box of reclaimed wood, a box of new lumber, or foam. Ask for close photos of the long face, the end, and any nail holes, mortise pockets, or checks. Ask whether the color is original patina or a stain on newer wood, and ask what the piece weighs. Ask whether it is sold as decorative. A beam that has to carry a load needs a builder or a structural engineer. Ask whether you will see photos of your exact piece before it ships.

Use the free quote form at https://barndobeamco.com/#quote, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Tell us the piece (a solid ceiling beam, a hand-hewn box beam, a mantel, or a table), the size, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US.

## Beam ideas by room

Where hand-hewn reclaimed beams, mantels, and custom beam tables go in a great room, a kitchen, at a fireplace, in a dining room, in an entry or on a covered porch, and in a bedroom. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-ideas-by-room

### How are hand-hewn reclaimed beams used on a great room or living room ceiling?
Run the beams the long way of the room and leave a clear gap for the fan and the lights. A tall great room can take a larger face, and a lower living room ceiling usually wants fewer beams or hollow box beams. For the face, the count, and the spacing, see the ceiling beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide.

Set the ceiling beams across the kitchen and stop them short of the hood, or run them beside it, so the hood and the duct stay clear. ### Can I use a reclaimed beam in an entryway or on a porch?

### How do I use a reclaimed beam in a bedroom?
Center one beam over the bed, running the width of the bed or a little past the nightstands, and keep it clear of the ceiling fan and the light. On a lower bedroom ceiling, a hollow box beam keeps the weight down and the face from crowding the bed. For solid versus box, see the ceiling beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide.

## Barndominium beam design guide

Where hand-hewn reclaimed beams work in an open barndominium: a tall great-room ceiling, kitchen and living zones marked by ceiling beams, a mantel scaled to a tall fireplace wall, a decorative header over a wide opening, and porch and entry accents next to metal and steel. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#barndo-beam-design-guide

### How do I use hand-hewn beams in an open barndo great room with a tall ceiling?
On a ceiling about 12 feet or taller, or across a wide open great room, use a 10 by 10 face so the beam reads from the sofa. An 8 by 8 is the usual face when the ceiling is about 9 to 12 feet. Run the beams the long way and leave a clear gap for the fan and the lights. On a vault, say whether the beams follow the slope or sit on the flat part. Wider spacing, about 6 feet on center with a 10 by 10, keeps a tall ceiling open. A hollow box beam is the lighter face on a finished ceiling. These beams are decorative unless a builder or a structural engineer approves one to carry a load. For the count and the spacing, see the ceiling beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide.

### How do ceiling beams define a kitchen and a living zone in an open barndo?
Stop the kitchen beams at the island, the end of the cabinets, or a change in the flooring, and leave the living ceiling with fewer beams or none. Or use about 3 feet on center over the kitchen and about 4 or 6 feet on center over the living room, in the same finish. Keep the beams clear of the range hood and the duct, and follow the clearance the range and hood maker require. Do not guess that number. For spacing, see the ceiling beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide.

### How do I scale a reclaimed wood mantel on a tall fireplace wall?
Keep the mantel at the height your local code and the fireplace or insert maker require. Do not raise it to fill a tall wall, and do not copy a height from a photo. On a tall wall, use a mantel plus two legs so the opening is framed. Add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side of the firebox. Twelve inches looks heavier on a big wall. A stock mantel has an 8 inch face and is 10 inches deep. See the mantel sizing guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-guide and the mantel install guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-install-guide.

### Can a decorative beam header mark a wide opening or doorway?
Yes, as a decorative accent. Measure the clear opening. Porch and entry headers are 8 by 10 or 10 by 12, in 6, 8, 10, and 12 ft lengths, and longer by quote. A longer run can be quoted as a ceiling-beam length used as a header. The header does not replace framing that carries a wall or a floor. Have a builder or a structural engineer handle anything that has to carry a load. A carpenter should do the install.

### Where do porch and entry beams work on a barndominium?
Use a header on a covered porch, under the roof, where rain does not hit the wood. Do not set a beam on an open deck. Inside the entry, use a beam console and leave walking room in front of it. For the porch finish and weather, see the beam care guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide. For the console size, see the coffee and console guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#coffee-console-guide.

### How do hand-hewn beams work with a metal or steel barndo interior?
Put a few hand-hewn beams where the eye already goes: the tall ceiling, the mantel, a header over a stair opening, and a porch header against metal siding. Natural or medium warms black window frames and a steel rail. Dark sits closer to black metal. Use the same finish on the beams and the mantel. Reclaimed wood will not match a paint color exactly. The beams are decorative.

## Range hood beam guide

How to size a hand-hewn reclaimed beam as a kitchen range hood mantel: hood width and overhang, face height and depth, clearance and heat, mounting, grease cleaning, and pairing with a mantel or ceiling beams. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#range-hood-beam-guide

### How do I size a hand-hewn reclaimed beam to a range hood?
Measure the range hood, outside edge to outside edge, not the cooktop. Add overhang on each side so the beam reads wider than the hood. Six inches looks tighter. Twelve inches looks heavier. A 48 inch hood plus 12 inches on each side is 72 inches, which is a 6 ft beam. A 36 inch hood is shorter than the 6 ft stock minimum, so a 6 ft beam leaves about 18 inches of overhang on each side when it is centered. If cabinets flank the hood, stop the beam short of the cabinet doors. Stock lengths are 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 ft. If the math lands between those, round up to the next length, or ask for a custom length. This overhang is for looks. It is not a heat clearance. See the range hood beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#range-hood-beam-guide.

### What face height and depth work for a range hood mantel?
A stock mantel from Barndo Beam Co. has an 8 inch tall face and is 10 inches deep. That is the usual hood mantel: tall enough to read above the hood, and deep enough for a short shelf that does not crowd the cook. A one-of-a-kind beam often has a face of about 8 to 10 inches. A taller face or a deeper shelf is a custom size by quote. On a wall with upper cabinets tight to the hood, an 8 inch face is usually enough. Tell us the hood depth and how much wall is above the hood when you request a quote.

### How much clearance does a wood beam need from a range hood?
Follow the clearance in your range hood manufacturer's instructions, and follow local code. A wood beam is combustible. If the manual and the local code do not match, follow the stricter one. Do not guess a number of inches, and do not copy a gap from a photo. The beam must not cover a filter, a light, or a control, and it must not pinch the duct. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood. The hood maker and local code set the clearance. Have the installer confirm the beam sits outside that clearance before the wood goes up.

### How is a range hood beam mounted?
A qualified installer should mount it. Three approaches are common, the same general approaches used for a fireplace mantel: a hidden steel bracket or rods in the back of the beam, a wood cleat lagged into the wall studs, or masonry anchors when the wall is solid brick or stone. The fasteners have to land in studs, blocking, or solid masonry, not in drywall alone. Leave the duct, the filters, and the hood controls clear so the hood can still be serviced. Do not fasten the beam to the hood unless the hood maker says the hood can carry that weight. A solid beam is heavy, and the beam is decorative. For the general mantel mounts, see the mantel install guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-install-guide.

### How do I clean cooking grease off a hand-hewn range hood beam?
Wipe grease with a soft cloth that is barely damp, and use a drop of mild dish soap if you need it. Dry the spot at once. Do not soak the beam. Do not use a steam cleaner, oven cleaner, bleach, or a harsh degreaser, because those can dull a natural, medium, or dark finish and lift color out of the adze marks. Work along the grain and leave the checks and tool marks. Do not sand the face. A finished beam is easier to wipe than a raw one. For everyday dusting, see the beam care guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide.

### How do I pair a range hood beam with a mantel or ceiling beams, and how do I request a quote?
Order the hood beam in the same finish as the fireplace mantel and the ceiling beams: natural, medium, or dark. No two pieces of reclaimed wood match exactly. Keep the ceiling beams stopped short of the hood, or run them beside it, so the hood beam is the piece at the range. Tell us the hood width, the beam length, the finish, and your ZIP code, and name the mantel or ceiling beams you want it to sit with. ## Character marks guide

How to read the character marks in a hand-hewn beam: scoring and hewing marks, mortise pockets, peg holes, old notches, nail holes, hardware stains, checks, and patina. Checks along the grain are normal seasoning, not a defect. Species and age vary by piece and are confirmed on the quote. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#character-marks-guide

### What do hand-hewn axe and adze marks look like?
Hand-hewn axe and adze marks are the cuts left when a log was squared by hand. Scoring marks are the first cuts: a row of axe cuts that set how deep the waste wood would come off. On the face they can read as a line of notches or as short diagonal facets. Hewing marks are the strokes that dressed the face. An adze leaves short scooped cuts. A broad axe leaves longer facets. The cuts overlap and change direction, so the face is uneven, with high spots and low spots, and the edges wander. A hewn face does not show a repeating circular saw arc or straight parallel saw lines. The end of a beam is often sawn square when it is cut to length. Read the long faces. The marks are there because the timber was shaped for a frame and the face was left as the tools finished it. See the character marks guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#character-marks-guide.

### What are mortise pockets, peg holes, and old notches on a hand-hewn beam?
A mortise pocket is a rectangular hole cut into the beam where the tenon of another timber sat. A peg hole is a smaller round or square hole where a wood peg locked that joint. An old notch is a step or a seat cut where a joist, a brace, or another beam landed. These marks are from the original timber frame. The cut is deliberate, and the edges are worn. It is not a break. Not every face shows a pocket or a notch. Some pieces show only tool marks and checks. Species and age vary by piece and are confirmed on the quote. Ask for a photo of the face if a pocket or a notch matters to you. See the character marks guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#character-marks-guide.

### What do nail holes and old hardware stains on a reclaimed beam mean?
Nail holes are the small holes left when nails or spikes were pulled. They can be round or square. Old iron often leaves a dark stain around the hole, or a streak where a strap or a hinge sat against the wood. The stain is in the grain. It is not dirt you wipe off, and it is not a sign the beam was damaged in shipping. Leave the holes and the stains. Filling them covers the history of the beam, and filler can pop out when the wood moves. For dusting without sanding the marks away, see the beam care guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide.

### Are checks and cracks in a hand-hewn beam a defect?
No. A check is a split that follows the grain. It opens as the wood seasons and dries, and a small crack along the grain is normal in reclaimed wood. It does not mean a decorative beam is failing. Wood also moves a little when indoor humidity changes, so a hairline check can open in the first heating season. Leave the checks. Do not fill them, and do not sand the face to hide them. A crack that runs across the beam, rather than along the grain, or a piece that arrives broken, is different. Send photos within 48 hours to barndobeamco@agentmail.to or call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326). For care, see the reclaimed beam care and finish guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide.

### How does finish change the character marks, and why don't two beams match?
Patina is the uneven color already in the wood: gray, amber, and brown, sitting on the high spots and down in the tool marks. A natural (clear) finish stays closest to that weathered color, so the scoring, the checks, and the color shifts stay easy to see. A medium finish warms the wood, and the marks still read. A dark finish deepens the grain. The facets and the holes still show, because the face is uneven, but the pale contrast is quieter. A finish does not plane the marks off. No two pieces match, because each beam is a different timber. Species and age vary by piece and are confirmed on the quote. Ask for photos of your actual piece with the free quote at https://barndobeamco.com/#quote. For how each finish behaves, see the beam care guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US.

## Measuring guide

How to measure for a hand-hewn beam, mantel, or table: fireplace firebox and surround, mounting height, depth, clearance to combustibles, ceiling length and width, slope, spacing, beam direction, a range hood, dining and coffee and console tables, and the photos to send with a quote. Clearance follows the fireplace or hood maker and local code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#measuring-guide

### How do I measure a fireplace for a hand-hewn mantel?
Measure the firebox width, the overall surround width, the mounting height, and the depth. Firebox width is the clear opening, inside edge to inside edge, in inches. Overall surround width is the finished stone, brick, or tile face, outside edge to outside edge. You need the surround width if you want a mantel plus two legs, so the legs land on the surround or just outside it. Mounting height is from the finished hearth, or from the finished floor if there is no hearth, up to where the bottom of the mantel will sit. Also note the height of the firebox opening. A stock mantel has an 8 inch tall face and is 10 inches deep. Measure how far the surround already projects from the wall, and how far you want the shelf to project past that face. Clearance to combustibles: a wood mantel is combustible. Follow the fireplace maker's instructions and local code. If they do not match, follow the stricter one. Do not guess a number of inches, and do not copy a gap from a photo. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood. The fireplace maker and local code set the clearance. For the length, add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side of the firebox, then match a stock length of 6, 7, 8, 9, or 10 ft. See the measuring guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#measuring-guide and the mantel sizing guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-guide.

### How do I measure a ceiling for decorative beams?
Measure the room length and the room width, wall to wall, in feet and inches. The direction the beams run is the beam length. The other direction is the width you space them across. Measure the ceiling height from the finished floor to the finished ceiling. If the ceiling slopes, measure the height at the low wall and the height at the ridge, and say whether the beams should follow the slope or sit on the flat part. Spacing is on center: from the center of one beam to the center of the next. Decorative beams are usually about 3, 4, or 6 feet on center. About 3 feet suits a kitchen. About 4 feet is usual in a living room. About 6 feet keeps a tall ceiling more open. Run the beams the long way and space them across the short way. Note which way the joists run. Beams usually run across the joists so a mounting board can fasten into them. Note lights, a fan, and any soffit the beams have to clear. Stock lengths are 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft. See the measuring guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#measuring-guide and the ceiling beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide.

### How do I measure for a range hood beam?
Measure the range hood, outside edge to outside edge, not the cooktop. Add overhang on each side so the beam reads wider than the hood. Six inches looks tighter. Twelve inches looks heavier. A 48 inch hood plus 12 inches on each side is 72 inches, which is a 6 ft beam. A 36 inch hood is shorter than the 6 ft stock minimum, so a 6 ft beam leaves about 18 inches of overhang on each side when it is centered. If cabinets flank the hood, measure the clear wall between the cabinet doors and stop the beam short of those doors. Also measure the hood depth, and the open wall above the hood, from the top of the hood to the ceiling or to the bottom of a soffit. A stock mantel has an 8 inch tall face and is 10 inches deep. This overhang is for looks. It is not a heat clearance. A wood beam is combustible. Follow the hood maker's instructions and local code. If they do not match, follow the stricter one. Do not guess a number of inches, and do not copy a gap from a photo. See the measuring guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#measuring-guide and the range hood beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#range-hood-beam-guide.

### How do I size a dining, coffee, or console table?
Size the table from the seats and the clear floor. For a dining table, allow about 24 inches of length per person. A rectangular table is usually 36 inches or 42 inches wide. Leave about 36 inches of walkway behind each chair so it can pull out. Four seats fit a 5 or 6 ft table. Six seats fit a 6 or 7 ft table. Eight seats fit an 8 ft table. Ten seats fit a 10 ft table. Twelve seats fit a 12 ft table. Measure the dining area, keep that walkway, and what remains is the largest top that fits. For a coffee table, use about 16 to 18 inches of height, level with the sofa seat or an inch or two lower. Make the length about one-half to two-thirds of the sofa, and leave 12 to 18 inches of walkway between the table and the sofa and on any side people walk past. For a console, a stock beam console is 32 inches tall. An entry console is often 4 to 6 ft long. A sofa-back console sits near the sofa back, about 28 to 32 inches tall, and runs about the length of the sofa or a few inches shorter. See the measuring guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#measuring-guide, the dining table guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#table-guide, and the coffee and console guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#coffee-console-guide.

### What photos should I send with a quote request?
Send three photos with the measurements. A wide shot shows the whole wall, fireplace, ceiling, or room. A close-up shows the wall or the ceiling where the piece will mount: the stone, brick, or tile, the drywall, or the joists if the ceiling is open. A third photo has a tape measure in the frame, extended across the firebox, the hood, the ceiling span, or the clear floor, with the numbers readable. Daylight is enough. The quote form opens an email. Attach the photos there, or send them to barndobeamco@agentmail.to with the measurements, the piece, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. See the measuring guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#measuring-guide.

### How do I send measurements for a free quote?
Use the free quote form at https://barndobeamco.com/#quote, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Include the measurements, the piece, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US. See the measuring guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#measuring-guide.

## Reclaimed wood indoors guide

Is reclaimed wood safe indoors? How dry old wood should be, acclimating a beam in the room for a few days, active insects versus old inactive holes, what to ask about drying and treatment, testing painted wood for lead, what a clear or natural finish does, and keeping beams off moisture and direct heat. This is general guidance. Ask about a specific piece when you request a quote. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#reclaimed-wood-indoors-guide

### How dry should reclaimed wood be before it goes indoors?
Old wood for a beam, a mantel, or a table should be dry to the room it will live in. Wet wood from a barn floor, a yard, or a recent rain does not belong on an indoor wall yet. In a heated home, indoor wood is often somewhere around 6 to 12 percent moisture content. The number moves with the season and the climate. A moisture meter is the practical check. The beam should read close to other wood already in the house, not soaking. This page does not set one moisture number for every climate. Ask us about drying when you request a quote. Before you install it, acclimate the beam in the room. Set it flat, indoors, and off a damp floor, and leave it a few days. A few days lets the surface settle to that room. A thick solid beam equalizes more slowly than a thin board. If the piece feels damp, or the house is very dry from heat, give it longer than a few days. Store the beam indoors, flat, and dry, and let it acclimate before it goes up. See the shipping and delivery guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#shipping-delivery-guide. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US.

### How can I tell active insects from old inactive holes in a beam?
Old reclaimed wood often has holes. Most of them are not a live problem. An old, inactive hole is dark inside, and the edge is worn, the same age as the rest of the face. No fine powder appears under the beam after you wipe the floor. A nail hole, a peg hole, and a mortise pocket are cuts from nails or from the timber frame. They are not insect tunnels. See the character marks guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#character-marks-guide. Active insects leave a different trail. Fine, fresh sawdust or small pellets keep showing up under the beam after you clean them away. New holes look pale inside, not dark and worn. You may see a live insect. Do not install that piece in a living space until someone who identifies wood insects has looked at it. Send photos when you request a quote and ask us what we know about that piece. A check is not an insect gallery. A check is a split that follows the grain as the wood dries. Leave it. See the reclaimed beam care and finish guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide.

### What should I ask about drying and insect treatment?
Ask whether the timber was dried for indoor use, how it was stored, and whether anything was done about insects. Old holes by themselves are not a drying record and they are not a treatment record. If those answers are missing, look closer. Ask us the same questions when you request a quote. Tell us the piece and your ZIP code, and ask about drying and about any holes you want to see in photos. We will tell you what we know about that piece. Use the free quote form at https://barndobeamco.com/#quote, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US. See the reclaimed wood indoors guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#reclaimed-wood-indoors-guide.

### Should I test old paint on reclaimed wood for lead?
Yes, if the wood still has paint and you plan to sand, scrape, or strip it. Paint on buildings from before 1978 can contain lead, and the age of a reclaimed beam is often unknown. Test any painted wood with an EPA-recognized lead test kit before you disturb the paint. The EPA lists recognized kits at https://www.epa.gov/lead/lead-test-kits. If the kit finds lead, do not sand that paint in the house. Follow the EPA's lead-safe work practices, or have someone who does that work handle the paint. Beams, mantels, and tables ordered from Barndo Beam Co. are finished natural (clear), medium, or dark. That finish is not a coat of old house paint. If a face still shows old paint, ask us when you request a quote, and test it before anyone sands it. This page does not claim a piece is lead-free.

### What does a clear or natural finish do on a reclaimed beam?
A natural (clear) finish is a thin clear coat with almost no shine. The weathered color stays close to the wood. The checks, the tool marks, and the holes still show. A spill beads instead of soaking in at once. That is the clear matte look in the beam care guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide. Medium warms the wood. Dark deepens the grain. A finish does not plane the marks off. A clear finish is not paint, and it is not a waterproof skin. Standing water still hurts the wood if you leave it there. The finish does not stop a check from moving when indoor humidity changes, and it does not change the clearance a wood mantel needs from a fire. Name natural, medium, or dark on the free quote at https://barndobeamco.com/#quote. Reclaimed wood will not match another finish exactly.

### How do I keep a reclaimed beam away from moisture and direct heat?
Use the beam indoors, or on a covered porch where the roof keeps rain off it. Do not set it where rain, a sprinkler, or standing water hits the wood. Keep it off a damp floor and off a known leak. Direct weather swells the beam, opens checks, and wears a finish off. Indoors, wipe a spill and dry the spot. Do not soak the wood. Keep the beam off a direct blast of heat. A floor register aimed at the wood, a radiator tight against it, or a lamp baking one face dries that face and can open checks. A wood mantel is combustible. Clearance to the fire follows the fireplace maker and local code. Do not guess a number of inches, and do not copy a gap from a photo. A clear finish does not make the beam heatproof. See the beam care guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide. To ask about drying, holes, or old paint on your piece, use the free quote form at https://barndobeamco.com/#quote, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Tell us the piece, the size, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US. See the reclaimed wood indoors guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#reclaimed-wood-indoors-guide.

## Finish matching guide

How to match a reclaimed beam to your floors, cabinets and trim: contrast or blend next to wood floors, painted cabinets versus stained cabinets, existing trim and doors, how daylight and warm or cool bulbs change a finish, using beams, a mantel, and a table together, why room photos help, and how to get a price and a shipping quote. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#finish-matching-guide

### How do I pick a beam tone next to wood floors, contrast or blend?
Blend when you want the beam in the same family as the floor. A pale or weathered floor sits closer to a natural (clear) finish. A warm mid-tone floor sits closer to medium. A deep brown floor sits closer to dark. Contrast when you want the beam to read as the feature. A dark finish against a lighter floor does that. A natural finish against a darker floor does that too. Hold a sample of the floor next to those three. The beam does not have to be the same board as the floor. Reclaimed wood will not match a floor stain exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. Name natural, medium, or dark on the free quote. See the finish matching guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#finish-matching-guide.

### How do I match a beam to painted cabinets versus stained cabinets?
Painted cabinets are a flat color, so the beam is the wood in that kitchen. Natural or medium keeps the weathered face easy to see against the paint. Dark sits closer to black paint and to black hardware. The beam will not match a paint chip. Stained cabinets are already wood. Pick the closest of the three finishes. A warm mid-tone stained cabinet sits closer to medium. A very dark stained cabinet sits closer to dark. A pale or grayed stained cabinet sits closer to natural (clear). They will not match exactly. The checks and the tool marks still show. For what each finish does, see the beam care guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide. See the finish matching guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#finish-matching-guide.

### How do I mix a beam with the trim and doors I already have?
Painted trim and painted doors can stay paint. The beam does not have to copy them. Use the finish you already chose for the floors and the cabinets, and let the painted casing read as paint. Stained trim and stained doors are a different piece of wood, and often a different stain, than the beam. Pick the closest of natural, medium, or dark. Natural stays closer to the weathered color. Medium warms the wood. Dark deepens the grain. If the doors are dark and the trim is painted a light color, decide which one the beam should sit with, then name that finish. Use that same finish on every beam, mantel, and table in the room. See the finish matching guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#finish-matching-guide.

### How does lighting change how a finish reads?
Look at the beam in the light the room actually uses. Daylight from a window shows the weathered color, the checks, and the tool marks most clearly. A natural (clear) finish stays closest to that color. Warm bulbs, the yellow household bulbs, pull the wood warmer. A medium finish looks more amber. A natural finish can look warmer than it did in daylight. Cool bulbs, the bluish ones, pull the same wood grayer. A dark finish can look flatter. A natural finish can look more gray than it did under warm light. Check the corner in daylight and again with the lights on before you name a finish. Tell us whether the room is mostly daylight, warm bulbs, or cool bulbs when you request a quote. See the finish matching guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#finish-matching-guide.

### How do I use several beams, a mantel, and a table together in one room?
Order them in the same finish: natural, medium, or dark. Ceiling beams, a fireplace mantel, and a dining, coffee, or console table can share that one finish. No two pieces match exactly, because each beam is a different timber. Say on the quote that they will sit in one room, and name the finish once. The match that matters among the new pieces is that they share a finish, even when the floors and the cabinets are a different wood. See the ceiling beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide, the mantel sizing guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-guide, and the finish matching guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#finish-matching-guide. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US.

### Why does sending photos of the room with a quote request help?
A photo shows the floors, the cabinets, the trim, and the light together. A color word does not. Send a wide shot of the room in the light you live with. Send a closer shot of the floor, and of a cabinet door or a piece of trim. Daylight is enough. If you can, send the same corner with the lights on. The quote form opens an email. Attach the photos there, or send them to barndobeamco@agentmail.to with the piece, the finish you are leaning toward (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We can tell you which of the three finishes sits closest. Reclaimed wood still will not match the floor or the cabinet exactly. See the finish matching guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#finish-matching-guide and the measuring guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#measuring-guide.

### How do I get a price and a shipping quote for a matched finish?
Use the free quote form at https://barndobeamco.com/#quote, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Include the piece, the size, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. Say if a mantel, ceiling beams, and a table should share that finish. Attach photos of the room: a wide shot in the light you live with, and a closer shot of the floor and of a cabinet door or a piece of trim. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US. See the finish matching guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#finish-matching-guide.
